checks: Actual fibers satisfy anchored compatibility. At an old deepest mark the own section of a containing active cap is proper. A positive margin at another deepest mark would permit a stricter cap while losing a positive slab at the original anchor, so all old deepest marks satisfy all old opposite inequalities.

The nonvertical tails are continuous with finite support ranges, and each strictly decreases just right of its old threshold. The rightmost positive-target inverse exists, exceeds the original threshold, and may jump only through plateaus. The old deepest marks retain own balls, and ambient interior points arbitrarily close to them give nonempty ambient interior.

The retained original band for every cap has mass a, including a=B up to null hyperplanes. Setwise coverage of C_a includes boundary-only and null fibers. Division by positive total mass supplies the normalized depth bound.

Monotone inverses and the union of m bands give m-Lipschitz total and per-fiber masses even across plateaus and at both endpoints. At zero every retained mixed point is on at least one old cap plane. Positive fibers are lattice-complete by anchored Minkowski combinations, and monotone continuous per-fiber mass yields finitely many entry events.

Rightmost inversion gives the exact strict exceedance correspondence. Local strictness at b_i supplies the a=0 marginal and M(B)=M handles the other endpoint. Counting the union via N_a and its excess proves both E identities and their monotonicity.
Read 92c5cf1d847ad56c §§1–3, (1)–(8). All statements use the original common cover and the summed d-volume rather than a new intrinsic measure at the zero core.

dependencies.hypotheses: The occupied bases of a compact convex body are finite and complete and its sections satisfy anchored compatibility. Positive M and positive old depth yield the required interior own marks, including exclusion of original null fibers as deepest sites.

overlap.comparison: It uses distal clipping for an atomless measure with convex support and a hereditary depth bound. This claim uses mixed fibers, rightmost inversion, retained deepest points, per-fiber birth and a full coupled overlap/rank path.
It bounds a volume-cover profile for ordinary full-dimensional volume using cap normal rank. It does not establish the coupled sampled-fiber path or its rank law.

readability: The rank variable is defined on the original measured mixed set. Its strict upper exceedance matches the closed retained body.
review_method: Independent proof read of the exact frozen candidate and check of its sources and predecessors. Exact rational replay for the distal and two-triangle numerical certificates.
summary: The rightmost distal inversion gives an actual convex path with full mixed-set cover, the stated Lipschitz laws, and exact rank and overlap identities, including the endpoints.
